items.name: chronytop
items.description: A TUI for chrony NTP time server monitoring
items.readme:
# chronytop

[![CI](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A TUI for [chrony](https://chrony-project.org) NTP time server monitoring, in the style of [btop](https://github.com/aristocratos/btop).

![chronytop demo](resources/chronytop.gif)

It graphs NTP requests per second, and shows server counters, the clients chrony is rate limiting the most, sources, tracking, bandwidth, and CPU and memory use (including chronyd's).

Panels resize with the terminal, and can be shown or hidden.

## Requirements

- Linux, with chrony 4.0 or later (`/usr/bin/chronyc`)
- Root (or `sudo`) for the server and offenders panels, or see [Running without root](#running-without-root)

chronytop is a single static binary with no dependencies outside the Go standard library, so it runs on any distribution (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL, Arch, Alpine, etc.).

## Install

Download the binary for your architecture from [Releases](https://github.com/geerlingguy/chronytop/releases), and install it:

```
sudo install -o root -g root -m 755 chronytop-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/chronytop
```

Or build it from source with Go 1.24 or later:

```
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o chronytop .
```

## Usage

```
sudo chronytop
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-i` | `1s` | Sample interval (500ms to 10s) |
| `-p` | `100` | Minimum packets for a client to be listed in offenders |
| `-version` | | Print the version and exit |

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `1`-`7` | Show/hide a panel |
| `+` / `-` | Slower / faster sampling |
| `?` / `h` | Show/hide help |
| `Esc` | Close help, or quit |
| `q` | Quit |

Visible panels and the sample interval are saved when you quit, to `~/.config/chronytop/chronytop.conf` (`/root/.config/...` when run with `sudo`), and restored on the next run. `-i` overrides the saved interval.

The offenders list is refreshed every 10 seconds in the background. chronyd filters clients by `-p` itself, so the list stays cheap to fetch on busy public servers with hundreds of thousands of clients.

## Running without root

Any user can see the tracking, sources, net, and system panels. The server and offenders panels use chronyd's `serverstats` and `clients` commands, which chronyd only answers over its Unix socket in `/run/chrony` by default.

**chrony 4.7 or later:** allow those two commands for local users with `opencommands` in `chrony.conf` (`/etc/chrony/chrony.conf` on Debian and Ubuntu, `/etc/chrony.conf` elsewhere). The list replaces the defaults, so it repeats them:

```
opencommands activity manual rtcdata smoothing sourcename sources sourcestats tracking serverstats clients
```

Then restart chronyd (`sudo systemctl restart chrony`, or `chronyd` on Fedora and RHEL) and run `chronytop` as any user. Only localhost can send these queries unless `cmdallow` says otherwise.

**Older versions:** adding your user to chrony's group (`_chrony` on Debian and Ubuntu, `chrony` on Fedora, RHEL, and Arch) only works if that group can write to `/run/chrony`, since `chronyc` creates its own reply socket there. Check with:

```
ls -ld /run/chrony
```

If it shows `drwxrwx---`, add your user to the group, then log out and back in:

```
sudo usermod -aG _chrony $USER
```

Debian and Ubuntu create the directory with mode `0700` (`drwx------`), so this doesn't work there; use `sudo` instead. Where it does work, it gives full access to chronyd's control socket, not just its stats, so members of the group can also step the clock or change sources.

## Security

Since it usually runs as root, chronytop:

- Only reads from `/proc` and `chronyc`, and never opens network connections.
- Only writes its settings file, and only if you changed a setting. It skips the file and its directories unless they're owned by the user running chronytop (so a non-root `HOME` under `sudo` is ignored), and saves through a temporary file, so it never follows a symlink.
- Runs `/usr/bin/chronyc` by absolute path, with a minimal environment and no shell.
- Strips non-printable characters from everything it displays, so data from chrony can't inject terminal escape sequences.

CI runs `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `gosec`, and `govulncheck` on every change.

## License

MIT

Aim suite for Rob Run — per-weapon presets, FOV control, bone priority and switch delay, all driven by profiles.

items.name: CVE-2026-123007
items.description: Proof-of-concept (PoC) scripts for CVE-2026-123007, an integer underflow in NGINX HTTP/2.
items.readme:
# CVE-2026-123007

## Overview

This repository contains proof-of-concept (PoC) scripts for CVE-2026-123007. For a technical analysis of the vulnerability, see the [Rapid7 blog](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-cve-2026-123007-critical-nginx-http-2-integer-underflow-leads-to-rce-fixed/).

The file [NGINX_HTTP2_STANDALONE_REPRODUCTION.md](NGINX_HTTP2_STANDALONE_REPRODUCTION.md) details the reproduction steps.

The file [simple-trigger-poc.py](simple-trigger-poc.py) is a minimal Python script to trigger the root cause issue.

The file [exploit/exploit.py](http://exploit/exploit.py) is a PoC exploit script to demonstrate unauthenticated RCE via CVE-2026-123007 against a vulnerable NGINX server running in a Docker container. This PoC is only suitable to demonstrate the given RCE exploitation strategy against a local freshly started Docker container. The PoC will likely fail against a vulnerable NGINX server which has multiple concurrent clients, or which has a "messy" initial heap layout (i.e. a worker process has been running and servicing requests for some time), where available network bandwidth is not sufficient to transfer the large amount of required data in a timely or consistent fashion, or where network proxying is in-place which may alter the exploits use of HTTP/2 frames. The PoC makes no attempt to account for these conditions. Alternative RCE exploitation strategies may be viable, but none are currently known.

## Example

The below video shows the PoC exploit achieving unauthenticated RCE against a vulnerable `linux/amd64` Docker image running NGINX version `1.31.8`.

![nginx-http2-rce-720p-8x.gif](nginx-http2-rce-720p-8x.gif)

items.name: NvidiaGsyncTweaks
items.readme:
# NVIDIA G-SYNC Tweaks

**Stop your G-SYNC / VRR monitor from flipping between 60 Hz and 120 Hz** - the cause of annoying brightness flicker on high-refresh OLED monitors
and of stutter at 60 FPS on 240 / 360 Hz panels - and tune the other hidden VRR settings of the NVIDIA driver, with a clear Windows 11 style interface.

![NVIDIA G-SYNC Tweaks - LFC page](docs/images/lfc.png)

## The problem

On high-refresh monitors the NVIDIA driver starts *frame doubling* (LFC) around **58-65 FPS**, long before your monitor's real VRR minimum (usually 48 Hz).
A game running at ~60 FPS then keeps jumping between 1x (60 Hz) and 2x (120 Hz). On OLED panels that shows up as flicker, on other panels as stutter. Frame-rate caps do not help,
and lowering the monitor to 120 Hz avoids it but throws away the high refresh rate.

The cause is a hidden driver setting, `vrrFrameSplitBehavior`. It was found and documented by u/PykeFeed in the
[Reddit thread "[Fix] NVIDIA G-SYNC kicks in LFC at ~60 FPS instead of 48 on high-refresh OLEDs"](https://www.reddit.com/r/OLED_Gaming/comments/1xtaqjo/fix_nvidia_gsync_kicks_in_lfc_at_60_fps_instead/).
This tool applies that fix for you - no registry editing - and shows what it will do to your monitor before you apply it.

## Download and install

1. You need Windows 10 / 11 (x64), an NVIDIA GPU with the NVIDIA driver (tested with 621.12) and the **Windows App Runtime 2.x**
   ([download from Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/windows-app-sdk/downloads)).
2. Download the zip from the [Releases page](https://github.com/Orbmu2k/NvidiaGsyncTweaks/releases), extract it anywhere and start `NvidiaGsyncTweaks.exe`.

No installer and no administrator rights are needed to start the app.

## Use it

1. Start the app. It finds your GPU and the driver's registry key by itself and shows what the driver does now.
2. On the **LFC / frame doubling** page choose **Lowest multiplier (recommended)**. The preview shows what your monitor will do, using your max refresh rate and VRR minimum.
3. Click **Apply & restart driver**. Windows asks for administrator permission (the shield on the button), your screens flicker for a few seconds, and the driver restarts - no reboot.

To check that it works, cap a game at 55 FPS: your monitor's refresh counter should show about **55 Hz** (before: about 110 Hz).

## What you can change

| page | what it is for |
|---|---|
| **LFC / frame doubling** | The fix: when does the driver start doubling frames? NVIDIA default, lowest multiplier, or your own stickiness - with a live preview, a table for other refresh rates, how fast the frame-time estimate reacts, and the frame-generation pacing switch. |
| **Smoothing & flicker** | How the driver evens out uneven frame times (a major cause of OLED VRR flicker). |
| **VRR behaviour** | Keep VRR always on, tearing behaviour, monitor detection over DisplayPort / HDMI, refresh limits. |
| **Cursor & idle** | What happens to the mouse cursor while a game is not delivering frames. |
| **Smart detection** | Experimental detectors for slideshow-like content and jittery frame times. |
| **Backups** | Restore points; one is created automatically before every change. |

Every setting shows its driver default, a *Changed* / *Custom* badge and a *Reset*. Settings that can cause trouble are marked **Use with care** or **Experimental**.

## Good to know

* **Restarting the driver** makes all screens go black for a few seconds and can crash running games, video or GPU programs. Close them first.
* **Undo:** use *Reset* on a setting, or restore a backup on the **Backups** page. The backups are plain `.reg` files in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NvidiaGsyncTweaks\Backups`.
* The switch point does not disappear, it moves to your VRR minimum. A game hovering right around 48 FPS can still flicker, and close to the minimum a late frame can cause a small hitch.
* Some VRR flicker is inherent to OLED panels at high refresh rates. This tool removes the part caused by the 1x / 2x switching.
* The settings are undocumented. NVIDIA can change or remove them in any driver update. A clean driver installation may reset them, a normal update keeps them.
* Made for NVIDIA GPUs with G-SYNC / VRR monitors (the Reddit thread has reports from GTX 16 to RTX 50 series cards). The settings apply to all monitors on that GPU. No effect on AMD or Intel graphics.

## Questions

**Why does it need administrator permission?** Only to write the settings to the registry and to restart the display driver. The app itself runs as a normal user; only that one step asks for permission.

**Where are the settings stored?** In the registry key of your graphics adapter: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\{4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}\000N`. The app finds the right `000N` through NVAPI and shows it at the top.

**Is it safe?** The fix itself is a single, well understood value. Every change is saved as a restore point first, and the app only ever writes the values listed in the interface. Still: it is an unofficial tweak of an undocumented driver setting - use it at your own risk.

## For the curious and for developers

* [How the driver decides - reverse-engineering notes for every value](docs/DRIVER-ANALYSIS.md)
* [Building, testing and releasing](docs/DEVELOPING.md)

items.name: wemail
items.readme:
# WeMail **本地优先的 AI 邮件客户端 —— 在你的电脑上同步、整理邮件,并接入你选择的 AI 服务。** **[访问项目网站 →](https://eddiezywang.github.io/wemail/)** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS-9cf.svg)]() [![Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/Electron-41-47848f.svg)]() [English](README.en.md) | 简体中文
--- ## 项目简介 工作邮件的真正痛点不是"收不到",而是"读不完、理不清、跟不住":每天上百封系统通知、审批流转和项目讨论混在一个收件箱里,重要信息被淹没,有价值的模式靠人肉规则勉强维持。 WeMail 把邮箱变成一个**本地优先的智能工作台**:通过 IMAP/SMTP 把邮件同步到本地 SQLite,由本机调度 AI 智能管线 —— 摘要、智能标签、回复草稿、待办提取,以及一个能替你读邮件、起草回复、执行操作的 Agent。AI 请求发送到你配置的模型端点,可能包含邮件元数据、正文和对话内容;使用远程端点时,这些内容会发送给该服务提供方。使用本地模型端点可在本机处理模型请求;遥测默认关闭。 它适合每天被工作邮件淹没、希望在本地获得 AI 辅助又不放心把邮箱交给云端服务的开发者与知识工作者。 ## 核心能力 ### 本地优先邮件引擎 **功能**:IMAP/SMTP 同步到本地 SQLite,由独立 utilityProcess 工作进程隔离运行。 **解决的问题**:邮件同步与本地缓存无需 WeMail 自营中间服务器；已缓存内容可离线阅读。 **价值**:本地保存邮件，断网时仍可查看已缓存内容。同步和发信依赖邮箱服务商，AI 与远程图片请求也可能访问外部服务。 ### AI 智能管线 **功能**:根据邮件类型和处理策略生成摘要、主题分类与待办事项；回复决策及条件满足时生成的草稿需要启用对应功能。 **解决的问题**:读不完的邮件流。 **价值**:辅助判断邮件内容和后续行动，减少阅读与整理成本。 桌面端默认关闭自动回复决策；设置 `WEMAIL_REPLY_DECISION_ENABLED=1` 后才会处理该类任务。功能输出还取决于模型配置、邮件类型和处理结果。 ### 用户可控的智能标签 **功能**:AI 从邮件内容中发现候选主题,经你确认后晋升为正式智能标签,并异步回填历史邮件。 **解决的问题**:传统规则易碎、纯 AI 自动分类不可信。 **价值**:AI 提议 + 人确认的混合模式,分类体系完全由你掌控、随时可改。 ### 带护栏的邮件 Agent **功能**:基于 Pi 运行时的助手,可读邮件、跨账户检索、起草回复、执行整理动作。 **解决的问题**:重复性的邮箱操作(归档、打标、催办、汇总)。 **价值**:硬性安全边界 —— 单次最多 6 轮工具调用、单工具 30s、单次运行 120s;发信及高风险操作需要确认。保存草稿和针对明确指定单封邮件的部分低风险操作可直接执行。 ### 自动化规则与洞察报告 **功能**:把重复模式固化为可编辑的自动化规则;日报 Digest;基于数据集的洞察报告(独立 HTML 产物)。 **解决的问题**:AI 每次从头理解的浪费,以及"邮箱发生了什么"缺乏全局视角。 **价值**:一次沉淀、持续生效;管理层视角的邮箱报表。 ### 企微 / 飞书机器人接入(可选) **功能**:把 Agent 接到企业微信 / 飞书群,流式回复(企微打字机、飞书卡片),支持群内审批待办动作。 **解决的问题**:不在电脑前时也能处理邮件事务。 **价值**:移动场景闭环,审批动作回到桌面端执行。 ## 效果展示

## 应用场景 - **每日邮件分诊**:早上打开邮箱,AI 已完成摘要与分类,按"待回复 / 待办 / 通知"快速过一遍,重点邮件给出回复草稿。 - **跨项目信息聚合**:同主题邮件自动聚成标签,配合日报 Digest 掌握各项目进展,不用翻聊天记录。 - **出差 / 通勤碎片处理**:企微 / 飞书机器人里让 Agent 汇总今天的重要邮件、起草回复,回办公室确认发送。 - **制度性邮件批处理**:审批流转、系统告警类邮件固化为自动化规则,自动归档 + 提取关键信息。 ## 安装部署 ### 环境要求 | 依赖 | 版本 | 说明 | |------|------|------| | Node.js | 22.19+（22.x）或 24.x | 构建 & 运行时；CI 使用 22.x | | npm | ≥ 10 | 包管理(随 Node) | | Bun | 使用与锁文件兼容的版本 | 安装根目录依赖 | | 操作系统 | Windows 10/11；macOS 待验证 | Windows 为主要开发平台，安装包仍需人工验收 | > 源码构建从 npm registry 拉取 Electron 二进制与原生模块(better-sqlite3 会按 Electron ABI 自动重建);内网环境建议先配置镜像。 ### 方式一:源码构建(标准) ```bash git clone https://github.com/eddiezywang/wemail.git cd wemail bun install --frozen-lockfile # 修补 pi-agent exports，并尝试准备 Electron 原生绑定 npm run build:desktop # 渲染层(Vite)+ 主进程/服务层(tsc)+ 运行时配置 npm run package:desktop # 使用项目打包脚本产出 Windows 未打包应用 ``` 如果安装时提示 Electron 原生绑定准备失败，请在启动或打包桌面应用前运行 `npm run ensure:desktop-native`。 ### 方式二:开发模式运行 ```bash npm run dev:desktop # Vite dev server + Electron 主进程热启动 ``` ### 验证源码 运行 `npm run verify:pr` 执行公开仓库的类型检查和测试。 ## 快速开始 ```bash npm run dev:desktop # 启动应用 # 1. 首页添加邮箱账户(IMAP/SMTP 地址 + 凭据) # 2. 设置 → 模型:填入你的 LLM 端点与 API Key(OpenAI / Anthropic 兼容) # 3. 等待首轮同步,智能管线自动开始工作 ``` ## 使用说明 - **邮箱连接**:设置 → 账户,支持多账户;凭据存入操作系统级加密存储(safeStorage)。 - **AI 配置**:设置 → 模型,BYOK(Bring Your Own Key);未配置时应用可正常收发邮件,智能功能降级。 - **智能标签**:邮件详情卡的候选主题 → "晋升为标签" → 确认名称与规则 → 历史邮件自动回填。 - **Agent**:侧边栏助手面板支持自然语言指令；发送和高风险操作需要确认，保存草稿及部分明确指定的单封邮件低风险操作可直接执行。 - **机器人**(可选):设置 → 连接,管理企微 / 飞书机器人连接。独立 LangBot webhook 路由当前未接入桌面 API，不能按回调入口使用。 - **MCP**:内置 MCP server，可把邮箱能力暴露给可信的本地 MCP 客户端（设置中开启）；持有连接凭据的客户端可执行写操作，无需应用内二次确认。 ## 系统架构 三层结构、单进程树,全部运行在本机:

- **渲染层**不直接触达任何外部服务,一切经本地 API;`shared/` 承载跨进程类型契约。 - **服务层**与主进程一起由 tsc 编译,无独立后端部署。 ## 核心工作流程 邮件从同步到智能产物的流水线: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[IMAP 增量同步
游标式] --> B[元数据入库
SQLite] B --> C[预筛
跳过系统退信等] C --> D[能力规划
按策略fan-out] D --> E[任务队列
租约+重试预算] E --> F[处理器按策略执行
摘要/标签/待办/可选回复决策与草稿] F --> G[(产物入库)] G --> H[渲染层实时呈现] ``` 关键设计:队列带**租约与过期回收**,AI worker 并发数可配(默认 2,上限 16),单条失败不阻塞整批;LLM 调用错误区分可重试/不可重试。 ## AI 工作流程 ### Agent 架构 ```mermaid flowchart TD U[用户指令 / 机器人消息] --> RT[PiAgentRuntime
6轮工具上限 · 120s运行上限] RT --> T1[只读工具
搜索/读取/汇总
自动执行] RT --> T2[高风险操作
生成待办动作] RT --> T3[保存草稿或单封邮件低风险操作
按策略执行] T2 --> PA[待办动作队列] PA -->|用户逐条确认| EX[执行器
动作参数不可篡改] EX --> Result[执行结果 + 审计日志] T1 --> RT ``` Agent 的发送邮件和高风险操作走"待办动作 → 确认令牌 → 执行"链路,执行参数与确认时严格一致。保存草稿和针对明确指定单封邮件的部分低风险操作可直接执行。可选 MCP 是独立权限边界：持有连接凭据的客户端可直接提交发送、移动和删除等操作，无需 WeMail 再次确认。 ### Prompt 管线 智能管线各处理器(摘要 / 标签 / 回复决策 / 草稿 / 待办)各有独立提示词,统一模式:**结构化输入(邮件元数据 + 清洗后正文)→ JSON 约束输出 → zod 校验入库**。标签体系分层:内置分类(固定)、用户智能标签(编译为分类提示)、AI 候选主题(仅提议,晋升前不影响历史组织)。 ### LLM 使用方式 - **完全 BYOK**:OpenAI 兼容或 Anthropic 兼容端点,Key 存于系统加密存储,调用模型时会发送给所配置的服务用于身份验证。 - 无任何内置模型转售;智能管线与 Agent 共用同一 LLM 配置。 ## 技术栈 | 层级 | 技术 | 用途 | 选型理由 | |------|------|------|---------| | 桌面壳 | Electron 41 | 窗口/托盘/更新/utilityProcess | 跨平台 + 多进程隔离 | | 渲染层 | React 19 + React Router 7 | SPA UI | 类型安全路由,SSR 同构能力 | | 状态 | TanStack Query 5 + Zustand 5 | 服务端状态 + 本地状态 | 缓存治理与轻量全局态 | | 样式 | Tailwind CSS 4 | 原子化样式 | 无运行时开销 | | 富文本 | TipTap 3 | 邮件编写 | 可扩展、协作编辑生态 | | 本地 API | Hono | HTTP 路由 | 轻量、类型推断好 | | 邮件 | imapflow + nodemailer | IMAP/SMTP | 成熟的协议实现 | | 存储 | better-sqlite3 | 本地数据库 | 同步 API,性能好 | | Agent | @earendil-works/pi-agent-core | Agent 循环/工具协议 | 硬护栏在运行时层实现 | ## 项目结构 ```text wemail/ ├── electron/ # Electron 主进程 + mail-core/db-service/bot-core 工作进程 │ └── main/ # 窗口、托盘、更新器、本地 API 启动 ├── server/ # 本地 API 与全部业务逻辑(Hono + TypeScript) │ └── wemail/ │ ├── bootstrap/ # 组合根:AppComposition 手写 DI │ ├── mail/ # IMAP/SMTP 提供者、同步服务 │ ├── intelligence/ # 智能管线:处理器、队列、智能标签 │ ├── agent/ # Pi Agent 运行时、工具集、待办动作 │ ├── channels/ # 企微/飞书机器人 │ ├── automation/ # 自动化规则引擎 │ ├── mcp/ # MCP server │ └── database/ # SQLite schema 与迁移 ├── app/ # React 渲染层(React Router 7) ├── shared/ # 跨进程 TypeScript 契约 ├── resources/ # 内置 Agent 技能与自动化模板 ├── tests/ # 渲染层与仓库脚本测试；服务端测试与源码相邻 ``` ## 配置说明 核心配置在应用内完成；常用开发与运维环境变量示例见 `.env.example`： | 变量 | 默认 | 说明 | |------|------|------| | `WEMAIL_TELEMETRY_*` | **空(禁用)** | 运行时遥测配置；下游构建也可包含 `build/telemetry-config.json`。安装包内的令牌可被提取，不能视为秘密 | | `WEMAIL_AI_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | 2 | 智能 worker 并发（1–16）；应用内保存的设置优先 | ## 安全设计 - **Agent 发信需确认**:草稿与 Agent 动作不会自动发送；可信 MCP 客户端可直接提交发信操作。 - **日志保护**:AppLogger 对已识别的敏感字段做脱敏；分享诊断信息前仍需检查并移除敏感内容。 - **远程图片**:打开邮件可能通过本机代理访问图片服务器，暴露网络地址及 URL 中的标识；已知像素过滤不能阻止所有追踪。 - **Agent 高风险操作需确认**:Agent 发信及高风险动作走确认令牌链路；MCP 客户端使用独立权限，不会触发该确认。 - **登出保留数据**:删除凭据但保留缓存邮件、智能产物与审计日志 - **留存策略**:当前不按固定天数自动清理邮件正文和附件缓存；应用日志默认保留 7 天，部分审计与自动化明细为 30 天，清理在应用运行期间执行。 - **遥测默认关闭**:环境变量和打包配置均未提供端点时不会发送遥测(见配置说明) 启用遥测时，事件会包含本机操作系统用户名、安装标识、应用及平台版本和经过校验的事件元数据，并发送到配置的端点。 ## 项目亮点 1. **隐私优先的 AI 邮件**:智能能力完整,BYOK,模型数据流向由所配置的端点决定 —— 与"云端读你邮箱"的产品形成根本差异。 2. **运行时硬护栏**:Agent 限制(轮数/时长/无发送工具/确认链)实现在运行时层,不依赖提示词自觉。 3. **混合智能标签体系**:AI 候选 → 人确认 → 规则沉淀 → 历史回填,兼顾自动化与可控性。 4. **单进程树完成全部隔离**:mail-core / db-service / bot-core 各自 utilityProcess,崩溃互不传染。 5. **桌面化改造完整**:从 Cloudflare Workers 架构完整迁移到本地优先架构,无云端残留依赖。 ## 贡献指南 欢迎 Issue 与 PR。开发环境见[安装部署](#安装部署),提交前请跑通 `npm run verify:pr`(schema 检查 + 三层 typecheck + 服务端单测 + 渲染层测试)。 ## FAQ **必须配置 LLM 才能用吗?** 不必须。未配置时邮件收发、浏览、搜索完全可用,智能功能(摘要/标签/草稿/Agent)降级隐藏。 **我的邮件数据存在哪?** 本机用户数据目录下的 SQLite,以及正文缓存。详见安全设计的留存策略。 **支持 Exchange / Gmail?** 支持配置 IMAP/SMTP 的邮箱；具体服务商可能有授权方式或兼容性要求，尚未逐一验证。专属协议（如 EWS）目前不支持。 ## License Apache-2.0。基于 [Cloudflare Agentic Inbox](https://github.com/cloudflare/agentic-inbox) 改造,遵循其原许可与署名要求,详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。 > 开源仓库 CI 覆盖类型检查、单元测试和桌面构建。浏览器及 Electron 端到端测试在独立环境维护，不包含在此仓库；发布前仍需进行安装包验收。

items.name: uberdesigner-studio
items.readme:
uberdesigner studio

Change your website's design one part at a time, with Claude, for 3 to 5× fewer tokens.

A Claude Code skill that turns a site into layers you can click, tweak and change,
in an editor that runs on your own computer.

Guide  ·  The numbers  ·  Discord  ·  uberdesigner.ai  ·  @bch1601 on X

## Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/bogdan239/uberdesigner-studio ~/.claude/skills/uberdesigner-studio ``` Then open your site's folder in Claude Code and say: ```text set up uberdesigner studio ``` Claude maps the site, installs the editor and gives you a link to open. ![The studio in Design mode: the site's layers on the left, the site in the middle with a numbered pin on a changed part, the AI changes on the right, and a box to ask Claude for a change](docs/assets/editor.webp) ## What it does - **Click a part of your site to pick it.** Headline, button, photo, section: each is a layer, listed like in a design file. - **Tweak it live.** Sizes, colours, fonts, spacing, timing and easing curves have sliders and pickers. Save writes the values into your own code. - **Type over any text** on the page. It goes straight into the file. - **Ask Claude to change that one part.** The request carries only the part's code, so it is fast and small. The result arrives as a card: keep it, undo it, or ask again. - **Go back any time.** Every change is a version in History. It works on a phone, tablet, desktop or large-monitor size of your site, side by side with the layers. ## Setting it up It needs Claude Code and Node.js on your computer. Setup checks both first and walks you through anything that is missing, one command at a time. **The best moment is right after Claude builds a site, in the same conversation.** Claude offers it by itself, and setup then costs about a third of doing it later (182k tokens against 529k on two sister test sites), because Claude already knows the site. ## Updating In Claude Code, say: ```text update uberdesigner studio ``` Claude checks GitHub for a newer version and, if there is one, gives you the one command that downloads it. Then it puts the new editor into the site you have open. Your map, History and change cards stay as they are. Each of your other sites gets the new editor when you say the same thing in its folder. What's new is in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## Works with - **Sites with no build step:** one HTML page, plain HTML, CSS and JS files, a site with its own small Node server, or a page made as a claude.ai Artifact. This is what Claude Code builds when you ask for "a website": 16 of 16 in our test. - **Vite + React + TypeScript** projects. Not yet: Next.js, Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, Vite without React. On those, setup stops before it reads or writes anything, and your site stays exactly as it was. ## The numbers We made the same 15 everyday design changes two ways: through the studio, and by asking Claude Code directly in a fresh copy of the site, with the same model. | | Through the studio | Asking Claude Code directly | |---|---|---| | Tokens for one change, in a new conversation | **10.8k** | **55.6k** | | Tokens for five changes, in one conversation | **58.7k** | **209.0k** | | Tokens those five changes add to your conversation | **0** | **41.4k** | | Time for one change | 8–32 s | 14–56 s | That is 3 to 5× fewer tokens per change: 5.2× in a new conversation, 3.6× in one that already knows the project. And a change through the studio adds nothing to your conversation, because it is a separate call outside your chat. This is our own estimate from a small sample: 15 changes on three of our sites, drawn at random, on 18 November 2026, with Opus 5.5. Tokens are weighted the way usage is priced. Setup is not counted: it costs tokens once per site. Results vary by project. The method, every number and the scripts are in [How we measure the savings](docs/methodology.md) and `backtest/`, so you can run it yourself. ## How it works 1. **A map.** Claude reads your site, and its build prompt if there is one, and writes down its parts in `inspector.map.json`. 2. **Labels.** Each part's element gets a small `data-dm="hero-title"` label in your code, so the editor and Claude mean the same thing by "the headline". 3. **The editor.** It runs on localhost next to your site: open the site's address and it opens in the studio. 4. **A change.** Asking for one sends your request with only the pieces of code that part needs (its markup, its styles, the scripts that touch it, the design tokens) to your own Claude Code, in one small call. What comes back is applied, checked, and shown as a card. 5. **History.** Every version is kept in a private folder inside `.inspector/`. Your own git is never touched. More in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md) and [Using the editor](docs/editor.md). ## What it adds to your project - **`.inspector/`**, ignored by git: the editor itself, History, and work files. - **`data-dm` labels** on your elements, and **`inspector.map.json`**. - **For Vite projects,** a few lines in `vite.config` that load the editor when it is there. A fresh clone without `.inspector/` still builds, and a production build never includes the editor. ## What leaves your computer The studio runs on your machine, and so does its server. Five things go out, and nothing else: - **Changes you ask Claude for.** The studio runs your own Claude Code with the request and the pieces of code it needs. That goes to Anthropic under your Claude account, as any Claude Code request does. - **The Google Fonts list.** When the font picker needs it, the server fetches the public list of families from `fonts.google.com` and keeps it for a week. No information about your site is sent. - **A font you pick.** Your browser loads it from Google Fonts, as the site will once the font is saved. - **An update you ask for.** "update uberdesigner studio" asks GitHub whether there is a newer version, and the command it gives you downloads it from there. Nothing about you or your site is sent. - **The "Explore 500+ Prompts" link** opens uberdesigner.ai in a new tab, after asking, and only if you click it. There is no analytics or telemetry in the studio. ## Good to know **What does it cost?** The studio is free. Changes made by Claude use your own Claude plan. Tweaks, History and most typed text use none of it. **Do I need to know the terminal?** No. Setup shows each command with a button to run it, and says what it is for. **Can I put it on a server for my team?** It is made for your own computer, with your own Claude account. Don't host it for other people or send their requests through one account. **What can't be clicked?** Objects drawn inside a canvas, such as a 3D scene. They can still be changed: pick them in the layers list. **My site changed outside the studio.** The editor says "The map is behind the site". Ask Claude Code to "update the uberdesigner studio map". **Old names.** The skill used to be called design-map and its editor the design inspector. What it puts in a site keeps the old word (`.inspector/`, `inspector.map.json`), so sites set up before the rename keep working. ## Docs - [Using the editor](docs/editor.md): everything in it, column by column. - [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): what a change sends, who can call the studio, what it writes and checks. - [How we measure the savings](docs/methodology.md): the test behind the numbers, in full, and how to run it. - [Measurements](docs/measurements.md): setup costs, what Claude Code builds by default, and the sites it was tested on. - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): what changed, newest first. For people changing the studio itself: - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to send a bug or a change, and what to run first. - [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): the pieces, how a change travels, and the rules the code keeps. - [Internals](docs/internals.md): how a layer is found on the page, picked, and brought on screen. - [Working on uberdesigner studio](docs/development.md): the folder, the stacks, the tests. - [SKILL.md](SKILL.md): the steps Claude follows when it sets a site up. - [Security](SECURITY.md): how to report a security problem. ## Why we built it We make design templates at [uberdesigner](https://uberdesigner.ai), and each one comes with the prompt that builds it. Building a site from a prompt takes minutes. The afternoon after it goes to small things: this button bigger, that headline lighter, the photo a little lower. Each of those sends the agent searching the whole project again. We wanted the part of a design tool that works for this: click the thing, change the thing. And we wanted Claude to get only the piece it needs, so a small change costs what a small change should. ## Community - **Bugs, questions and ideas:** open an issue. A security problem goes [another way](SECURITY.md). - **Prompts to build from:** the [uberdesigner library](https://uberdesigner.ai/library). - **Discord:** [join the uberdesigner server](https://discord.gg/CuyTccfBg3). One click, and you don't need an account on uberdesigner.ai. Ask for help, show what you made, tell us what to build next. - **What changed:** the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). For news and what's next, follow [@bch1601](https://x.com/bch1601) on X. ## Licence Copyright 2026 Advanced Design Technologies Ltd. uberdesigner studio is open source under the [GNU Affero General Public License, version 3](LICENSE) (AGPL-3.0-only). In short: you can use it, change it and share it, in commercial work too. If you give a changed version to other people, or let them use one over a network, you offer them that version's source under the same licence. The licence's own text is what counts, not this summary. - **Your site stays yours.** Working on a site with the studio doesn't put the site under this licence. What you publish holds none of the studio's code, only the `data-dm` labels on your elements. - **The credit stays.** Every shared version, changed or not, keeps the notice the editor shows: "uberdesigner studio. © 2026 Advanced Design Technologies Ltd." The exact term is in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). - **Contributions are welcome:** see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Before an outside contribution is merged, we ask its author to sign a contributor agreement, so that Advanced Design Technologies Ltd. can keep offering the studio under this licence and others. - **The typeface** in the editor, Instrument Sans, is under the SIL Open Font License (`runtime/panel-src/fonts/OFL.txt`). - **"uberdesigner"** and its logo are trademarks of Advanced Design Technologies Ltd. and aren't covered by the licence. ---

Made by Bogdan Chechin and the team behind uberdesigner.
